chunks: 1669 - And in the narration of ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

"Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله accepted the jizyah from the people of the dhimmah on the condition that they would not consume usury, would not eat the flesh of swine, and would not marry sisters, nor daughters of a brother, nor daughters of a sister. So whoever among them does that, then the covenant of Allah and the covenant of His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله is absolved from him."
And he said: "Today, they have no covenant."

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: the people living under the protection and covenant of the Islamic polity
key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury or unlawful gain through interest-based increase
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةَ: the poll tax accepted from non-Muslim protected subjects under covenant
key_terms.ذِمَّةُ اللَّهِ: the covenant and protection of Allah
key_terms.ذِمَّةُ رَسُولِهِ: the covenant and protection of His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: Under what conditions did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله accept jizyah from Ahl al-Dhimmah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله accepted jizyah from Ahl al-Dhimmah under specified conditions relating to prohibited acts in financial conduct, food, and marriage. It further states that violating those conditions nullifies the dhimmah covenant, and concludes with the statement that they do not have dhimmah today.
